paragraphs.source_en: Mehmed IV’s successor was to be Suleiman, his forty-fiveyear-old younger brother. But Suleiman, too, was terrified of being killed. He refused to come out of the harem. Breaking down from decades of anxiety about this moment, he asked whether the officials summoning him could understand what it was like to spend a life in terror, how ‘it is better to die at once than to die a little each and every day’, and began to cry.'* He had nothing suitable to wear for the enthronement. The chief eunuch put his own sable over Suleiman’s robe. Thus dressed, he became Suleiman II (reigned 1687-1691), as his brother Mehmed IV, his other brother Ahmed, and the two princes Ahmed and Mustafa were put under house arrest. Mehmed IV died of natural causes six years later. The sedentary sultan had returned.
